sentences.text:
The Honourable Sri Justice K.Sarath
 Writ Petition No.5967 of 2023
Order:

This Petition is filed for the following relief:
"...to issue a Writ order or orders particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the respondents in constructing road from the petitioners land bearing Survey Nos.1096 1098 and 1100 of Auvuslonipally village, Wargal Mandal,
Siddipet District without following due process of law arbitrary, illegal and violative of the Article 14, 16, 21 and 300-A of the Constitution of India and also in violation of provisions under Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: consequently direct the respondents not to construct the road from the petitioner land..."

2. Heard learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Panchayat Raj and Rural Development appearing for the respondent Nos.1 to 3, learned Standing Counsel for Gram Panchayat appearing for the respondent No.4 and perused the material on record by.
3.

Learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are the owners and possessors of the lands in Sy.Nos.1100, 1098/A1/2/1 and 1092/AA, admeasuring ::2::
Ac.1.22 guntas, Ac 1.08 guntas and Ac.2.07 guntas respectively situated at Auvuslonipally village, Wargal Mandal, Siddipet District.

While the matter being so,
the respondents proposed to construct C.C. Road from the lands of the petitioners under the Scheme of Food for Work.
Subsequently, the petitioners objected for the said construction on the ground that there is an alternate road, which can be utilized for the said road.

Without considering the objections raised by the petitioners and also without issuing any notices, the respondents trying to dispossess them petitioners from their respective lands without following due process of law.
Aggrieved by the action of the respondents, the petitioners filed the present Writ Petition and requested to allow the same.
4. Learned Standing Counsel for the respondent No.4, basing on the counter-affidavit, submits that there is no encroachment into any of the patta lands of the petitioners herein.

The proposed C.C.
road has not been laid by the respondent No.4/Gram Panchayat and it was only a preparation for laying the said road.

He further submits that ::3::
the respondent No.4/Gram Panchayat proposed to lay the said C.C. road in the existing Kacha Bata, without encroaching into any of the patta lands as claimed by Mothe Venkavva vs The State Of Telangana on 5 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147703660/
1 the petitioners herein and requested to dismiss the writ petition.

sentences.text: 5. Having regard to the submissions made by the learned counsels for both sides, this Court is of the considered view that the writ petition is disposed of, directing the respondents not to dispossess the petitioners from their respective lands without following due process of law.

If the respondents wants to acquire the lands of the petitioners, they have to follow the procedure as contemplated under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

sentences.text: However, there shall be no order as to costs.
6. Miscellaneous Applications, if any pending in this writ petition, shall stand closed.

opennyai_summary.decision:
